title: Warhammer 40,000: Kill Team
text: This is an arcade twin stick shooter basically, although I couldn't play it with my joypad (not an Xbox gamepad). You can as well play it with keyboard and mouse. You pick one of four space marine specialities - melee, ranged, librarian and techmarine. There are only two differences between those classes - special attack and one weapon that you can change when unlocked. The plot is pointless, basically a one man killing machine destroys an orc space ship and kills thousands of orcs and tyrranids. I've finished it with a Techmarine in under three hours. Pros: - Warhammer 40k aesthetics - you can play it in co-op - you can unlock bonuses and additional weapons Cons: - camerawork - some levels are absurd in design - e.g. you are in a central hub and need to go back and forth to every one of four nodes - it gets monotonous really fast - weapons feel as if they were not that powerful - it takes about 3-4 shots from bolter gun to kill a standard orc. Or maybe those enemies are that tough? - you can have only one powerup at a time - powerups last too short - classes are not well balanced - I think that ranged class is the most powerful because you can deal heavy damage from distance while avoiding taking hits when engaging in melee - special skills are dull - techmarine creates an automated shooting tower, melee class is charging on enemies ending the charge with explosion, ranged class has speed up to rate of fire (most useful imo) and librarian is creating a sucking vortex around himself that explodes after about 2 seconds Overall I feel that this may have been a good game but it lacks polish. Levels are too long, shooting orcs and tyrannids gets boring after about an hour. Maybe it is more fun in co-op, but I haven't played it this way. You can play it for a dollar or two, but I would not invest more money into this title. Space Marine game is a better shooter/slasher set in the Warhammer 40k world. ---------- For anyone interested in joining in on completing your own backlog; check it out here -

title: Warhammer 40,000: Kill Team
text: This is not a good game. Story's not too bad, although there's not much there. Graphics and aesthetics are fine. Really, what makes this game so bad is the gameplay. The mouse sensitivity and keyboard are laggy and unintuitive. There are no crosshairs to see where your going to be shooting. And the camera. The camera. The camera angles are these terrible, completely set points, and very often you will get stuck in a corner firing blindly offscreen hoping, just hoping, that you will hit something. There are plenty of good 40k games out there. Don't waste your money on this one.

title: Warhammer 40,000: Kill Team
text: Boring Repeative and Buggy Kill Team is a twin stick shooter set in the 40k universe where you play a space marine kill team trying to take down an ork crusier.  There is very little in the way of story beyond this.  you will be told to go somewhere and blow somthing up or kill somthing until you fight the warbosses at the end and thats it. The game is basic as hell. you pick one of four classes and mow or chop down dozens of orks and eventually tyranids.  Occasionally you pick up power ups or spam a charge attack special move to help with the hairier situations and thats about it.  Its mostly move from point A, killing everything on the way to point B, where you will fight several waves of enemies or one of three bosses.  The enemies boil down to either melee or ranged mobs with varing degrees of health and none of them feel unique from one another. the two melee and two ranged classes barely feel different from one another save for their special move and you don't really level up. rather getting points unlocks passive buffs and eventaully more powerful main weapons for each class. No skill tree or unlockable special moves.  You can pick from several space marine chapters but all this does is change your color scheme. The game is really short too. only about 6 or 7 missions that will take you about 30 mins each to beat.  There are unlockable surivial modes but with only a hand full of perks and weapons to unlock why bother? On top of all this the game is kind of buggy.  During the opening cutscene ugly green pixilated spots appear all over the screen.  i've had the game crash a couple of times losing my progress in a mission and while you can aim in the general direction of the enemies the game automatically aims up or down when your on uneven ground or if your being rushed by small enemies...or at least its suppose to but in practice i usally ended up shooting over or under the enemies and taking hits.  This is espcially noticeable with the the sternguard veterans missle launcher which has a slow rate of fire so every miss is a big deal when your swarmed.  And the game can be really cheap as eneimes can eat your health in seconds (especially the terrorguants), checkpoints are spread too far and the camera is fixed and will somtimes suddenly shift in the middle of battle or even get stuck in places. This is a boring and at times frustrating slog of a game.  You might get a little fun out of it if you play with a friend but there are way better twin stick games and certianly better 40k games out there.  I'd say skip this game even if its on sale.

title: Warhammer 40,000: Kill Team
text: Being a huge fan of the Warhammer Fantasy and 40K franchises, I ended up buying literally all games during the Warhammer sale a few months ago. Warhammer 40K: Kill Team is one of the massive letdowns within the franchise. It has close to no character progression, little to none in regards to equipment customization, very little content, a dodgy and oversimplifiedly boring combat system, clipping errors as well as abysmal graphics. The only redeeming feature is the ability to play the entire campaign in co-op, but then again I don't know why anyone should want to do that, as there are scores of other games out there which are a lot more fun together. Even diehard Warhammer fans will have a hard time liking this entry. I wasn't one of them. Can't recommend it to fans either and especially can't recommend it to the general public.

title: Warhammer: End Times - Vermintide
text: Intriguing online Co-op game set in the Warhammer universe that can be played for hundreds of hours if you are into horde shooters. This game is an fps, rpg, hack and slash mixed in a level clearing/objective completing fantasy world. It also has a story told within the levels, but gets omitted once you repeat the same levels for loot and challenges. The levels with its various completion requirement coming with different difficuly options will give the player quite a challenge since the requirements for getting better loot depends on the amount of tomes and grimoire collected throughout the run. Since the tomes and grimoires replace slots for potions and grenades, the game becomes a mix of resource management and selection of perks for its 4 man co-ops. Overall a great co-op horde game and one of the better warhammer games we have  in the gaming community.

title: Warhammer: End Times - Vermintide
text: 7/10 in its current state (week after release). The graphics and theme are excellent. If you are a fan of Warhammer themed games but, like me, tired of seeing the genre getting butchered and shoehorned into a lot of crappy games, you're in luck. Vermintide takes the Warhammer theme and uses it well, doing it the justice it deserves. You will feel immersed. Gameplay: Similar to L4D but better. You pick a level from the hub (a tavern) and run it with 3 other players or AI. You'll encounter all sorts of enemies from numerous packs of skaven warriors and swarms of slaves through to elite lone gutter runners or troops of stormvermin. The pace is pretty fast, but you do get time to breathe and enjoy yourself too. The combat is satisfying, but RIP if your ping is high and you're trying to use a ranged weapon. What could make it better? If they fixed some bugs, optomised performance, and tightened it up a little this would be 8/10 from me. With some extra content, maybe 8.5/10. The final 1.5 points deducted are due to the fact this game is always about frantic online gameplay in the same mode. It lacks diversity. There is no slower paced exploration, duelling, singleplayer little challenges and levels etc. I know it's a lot to ask, but the fact is it won't scratch all your itches. You'll crave other gameplay after a time. Still, 7/10. I consider this game fairly solid (minus the points discussed above) and good co-op fun.

title: Warhammer: End Times - Vermintide
text: Unfortunatly level design and rewards contradict each othe too much (e.g. a short level rewards you as much as a longer and harder one). Furthermore most maps feature boring design and you will soon end up grinding that one map that doesnt suck and gives you quick rewards. Classes do not posses any skills which would further differentiate them from one another. Unfortunatly also a pure button masher and not a great melee combat sytem like in dark messiah. A lot of potential unused... Oh and did I mention picking up barrels as objective in almost every level is ♥♥♥♥ing boring? Oh and not to mention crashes (yup you just ♥♥♥♥ed your party, thx random crash, and nope you wont rejoin cause someone will join the game in your stead as you can't reserve single slots) and horrible performance on some maps/ and certain effects. Oh and who doesnt want to get butt♥♥♥♥ed by rng at the end of a hard level receiving the same loot with all bonus enhancers you would receive on the lowest difficulty. Also there are several ways to cheese the levels atm which are heavily being abused by the community, which lead to a huge gap in gear for those who do not make use of the possibilites the game currently offers. There are levels where you can completly block enemy spawns no matter what the difficulty level and which are just broken in their current state. Also there are several bugs (e.g. resolution reset on startup) and more crashes than i think are acceptable for a launch title. Just to give a comparison: In the past 5 years not one launch title I played crashed as many times as warhammer did! Sry for the long rant there are of course also things I like about the game but I think the other reviews cover that in enough detail, overall I still would hold of and wait for the game to either be patched some more or on sale, as I do not think they will be able to fix the design issues any time soon.

But in the end it has two main limitations: 1) It is exactly the same as the first Warlock, so what's the point of making (and buying) another game? 2) The basic idea is Civilization with magic, but the final result is a game that tries really hard to be too many things at the same time and does not excel at any. As a 4X it is quite limited and superficial; it tries to have magic take the place of historical depth, but it fails, also because any form of world's lore behind the quest is completely absent; the presence of missions could have given some RPG flavour, but they mostly fall flat. In conclusion, it is not a bad game, but I cannot really recommend it, especially if you already own the first one and did not love it to pieces.

title: Warlock 2: The Exiled
text: This game is Warlock 1 with an expansion pack. It has more races, more building and unit options, and an improved interface but they aren't really enough to make it a game in its own right. The main scenario is interesting but it suffers from the issue that many strategy games do where they compensate for the AI being a bit dumb by throwing huge numbers of units at you instead. As you approach the finale, 10 or so high level units randomly spawn across your lands every turn making that part of the game a frustrating grind. title: Warlock 2: The Exiled
text: Fun game. Essentially Warlock 2 is Civilization V with a fantasy twist, and the twist makes all the difference. Never enjoyed Civ 5, but I am liking Warlock a lot. Warlock 2 does a great job at making you feel like a badass mage, packing some powerful spells like the ability to warp the landscape and erect a volcano, or call in a lightning storm, and grant your troops the ability of flight. There's also a fun quest system, and NPC mages that will harass you until you complete certain quests. If you never played the first one, then this is a great game to pick up. Most of the negative reviews come from people who felt Warlock 2 didn't add enough to Warlock 1 to justify the "2," but it's nevertheless a good game. Contrasting to AoW3, then I find that AoW3 does everything better than Warlock. More customization, more detailed battles, more maps, two length single player campaigns (Warlock has none), and a better selection of avatars. However, you might still prefer Warlock over AoW because Warlock is more streamlined for quicker turns and games. It's probably, therefore, a better choice for multiplayer, unless you want long drawn out games amongst close friends with AoW3. All in all, if you're an impatient player, you might prefer Warlock, but either way you can't go wrong.

title: Warlock 2: The Exiled
text: The problem with Warlock 2 is not that it's a bad game; rather, it doesn't add enough to justify the 'sequel' tag and $30 price point.  Exiled mode is merely a focused string of 'pocket dimensions' (that already existed in the first game) in a campaign format -- no more innovation than the Armageddon mode for Warlock 1.  The other improvements and additions are arguably ones that should have been included in a patch or, at most, a $10 DLC.  Unrest is the only truly new mechanic and its implementation is primarily intended to cap the number of cities you can build.  This ultimately has little bearing on the game as you can win on even the hardest difficulty with a few lords and a couple of complimentary units. The Great Mage edition for $50 is particularly laughable as it merely adds a few lords I've never even seen in 30+ hours of play, a few spells I've never bothered to cast, and a dragon mage hero that doubles as a capital -- the latter being the only one I'd recommend buying separately for a couple of bucks.  The other extras are a bunch of out-of-game materials most people won't listen to/read. Edited: And now in the recent patch they've added an in-game store selling things like the privilege of starting on a certain plane/shard for $3.  Warlock 1's Armageddon DLC cost the same and added a new mode.  The Elf DLC added a new race for the same price.  Paradox is definitely on the decline with all these cash grabs.

title: Watch_Dogs® 2
text: It's pretty good. (I didn't play WD1 so this review is based of WD2 all on its own.) So, the hacking. Oh, the hacking. Lovely game mechanic that genuinely switches up gameplay in its own way. Hacking cars and such while roaming or hacking headsets to flood a dudes ears with static, it's solid. Which is good, because the shooting is absolute garbage. Couldn't tell you how it compares to GTA 'cause I don't own it. I played without aim assist, which may have been a mistake. There's an ending sequence that I'll forever hold as a What Not To Do example where . The game gives you all the best guns, but it took me at least 8 tries on Normal difficulty. If that isn't an easy example of bad game design then I don't know what is. The kicker is that I finally succeeded by sneaking around as much as possible, using the one-hit-kill overlong pre-animated melee attack to snub anyone who wandered too close. On the upside, the driving is Really Good. For real. Like on par with The Crew (haven't played any other car games lately so that's my only point of reference). All the vehicles handle noticably different, which motivates you to drive different ones and buy a certain model. You can summon, free of charge, with one of the many custom painjobs available, any car you buy at a dealership. There's one bugbear where my steering would occasionally lock up and I'd veer into a wall. Only happened like 4 times total tho. Weird. But driving, with the quick hacking and the sturdy police cruisers, is probably the highlight of the game. Ubi's 'seamless' multiplayer is probably the best it's ever been. The best part: There are options to allow/deny individual online shenanigans. I wasn't a fan of the invasions but I loved Bounty Hunt, for example. It's quite pretty, and props Ubi for releasing a 4K texture pack as free DLC, but I had stutters and hangs on medium-high graphic settings. Had a few freezes, but no more than anything Beth has made. Might be a small memory leak. The story... well it's . The main story threads were interesting enough to drive me through the story mode. The side missions are probably the better designed, though. Not as interesting, but typically use certain facets of the game to show how good it can be. It all sounds like it was written by the Corporate who haven't looked out a window since the Matrix was showing in theaters, but the voice acting and mocap is generally above par. Not quite Witcher 3 standards, but better than a lot of other games recently. The ending was kinda lackluster, even with the aforementioned bit. There were a couple plot twists that had all the impact of a pebble thrown into a raging river. The whole thing felt too short: when the little prompt "This is the Final Mission" popped up I was like, "What? For real?" and yeah, for real. You can wander afterwards, Skyrim style, but Ubi sandboxes are pretty bland without a story to willfully ignore. The game is at it's best when you're bouncing around between the cameras and your drones to outwhit better-armed enemies. The game suffers, badly, whenever it forces you into a shootout. The story is lackluster and feels like it ends before it . The driving is brilliant, to the point you can probably play this instead of The Crew. Wait for a sale, then pick it up, for sure. It's overall a good game (7/10) and redeems the Watch_Dogs franchise, but it's far from perfect.

title: Watch_Dogs® 2
text: ***MINOR SPOILER*** I hated this game at first. Working in tech, the preposterous nature of everything was hard to swallow, and then the fact that there ARE NO CONSEQUENCES FOR KILLING INNOCENT PEOPLE IN THIS GAME really threw me off.  As many other reviewers have lamented about the number of lethal options available and encourage players to play non-lethally. It grew on me though.  The voice acting was excellent, and learning about the characters and their story and their quirks really felt natural. Then, there was the spider-bot sequence. I had never heard "The Day is My Enemy" by Prodigy until this game, and I am a huge Prodigy fan.  So when the song came on, too quiet, in the background, and the level opened up in to a (VERY obvious pandering sequence) of security guards shooting at me, I was IN.  INVESTED.  I felt like a sweet♥♥♥♥♥counter-culture hacker driving a 12-ton 8 legged mass of high-tech PAIN through an obstacle course of exploding cars. And then I jumped. The thing ♥♥♥♥ing jumps.  Not only does it jump, but it STICKS TO WALLS AND CEILINGS AND YOU WALK ON THEM.  WHAT.  THE.  ♥♥♥♥.  I FLIPPED out when I saw this and yelled "♥♥♥♥ YEAH!!!" at my computer monitor. Creating moments like this are why people make games, and Watch Dogs 2 did that for me. Overall, I could see that it suffered from the classic fun vs. realism dichotomy that so many games have issues with; the devs at Ubi decided to err on the side of "fun" a lot more than "realism" and that was disappointing to me in the context of a set of characters I was supposed to care about. The biggest detractor is that when your motivation for doing something in a game is to protect the privacy and quality of life of innocent people with complicated situations, and you straight up murder them all the time in the name of that, it really detracts from the purpose and sense of realism and investment.  I would have loved to have seen story-based consequences for use of lethal force.

text: I was one of the few people that actually enjoyed the first Watch Dogs, even though I agree that Aiden was a boring character and the story had massive issues and lack of any realism. Watch Dogs 2 takes another turn, a less serious, silly game about hackers. The game is still open world and filled with tons of events, the hacking are also very similar to the first game although expanded. The story is filled with references to movies and games and mocks the nerd culture, in a good way. Some characters might be too much though but I find it pretty good most of the time. If you are expecting a serious game this won't be up your alley. The driving is improved from the first game but I would say that it still needs some work to be perfect. The graphics are looking good. You can download a ultra texture pack from the steam store for free that lets you upgade the look even more. It runs well and Ubisoft did an great job with the PC port. I tried to play both with xbox controller and keyboard + mouse, both worked well although I prefered the contoller for driving. There's so much to do in the open world. I feel like I dont wanna do all of it, but I get that some people do. I did everything in the first game but now I'm more burned out on the open-world games. This title got all the usual ubisoft open-world stuff for anyone interested, enemy areas, loot, upgrades and so on. But with the amount of other games I wanna play I wont be 100% this title just for that reason. It's more of the same but It can add hours to your playthrough if that is what you are looking for. I'm personally just playing through the story. There's a lack of non lethal weapons but I heard that Ubisoft is adding more of them for free, which is nice. You can of course also use normal guns but they make noise that alerts the enemies. I had fun using a few different ones and they have expanded the guns I think. The combat is alright but it doesn't feel as satifying as in some other action games in my opnion. I really liked the music in the game from the radio stations. I listened to them all for a bit and I especially liked the rock personally. The sound overall is good. Watch Dogs is a solid game, not much to complain about. Maybe the fact that people can join you from nowhere and try to kill you. I get the fun aspect of it, but its also silly to have both the police and some online people trying to kill you. I do think you can turn it off though, but it is on by default. They have a level system for joining other players, killing them or doing objectives. I have seen some people only playing that and it can be pretty fun. Personally im just in it for the single player aspect and the story. Recommended game for people who like open-world games. Just remind yourself that this is not a "dead serious" game like the last one. This game doesn't take itself serious and mocks itself and a lot of games and movies. Hackers are more of a silly thing in this game, but gameplay it is mostly the same, but improved. A good but not perfect title in my opinion.

title: Watch_Dogs® 2
text: I really enjoyed Watch_Dogs 2. I held the unpopular opinion when Watchdogs 1 came out that it was better than GTA V. For me personally I just had more fun with it than GTA V, which I also thought was a very good game. I hold the same feeling for Watchdogs 2 but even stronger. Many people had an issue with the main character, Aiden Pierce, that he was bland and flat. I believe that they made the right decision with Watchdogs 2 with its main character, Marcus. He's much more enjoyable and humorous, as his most of the supporting characters. This is actually a common thing that I loved about the game. The world is lighthearted and funny, with a serious moment every now and then but few and far between. It tackles issues with the modern technological landscape and society using satire, more effectively than GTA does in my opinion. As for the gameplay, it has improved however oddly enough even though I think Watchdogs 2 is a much better game than the first, it took out some good features that were in the first game. For example, you could rob stores in the first game and had a noteriety level. That's gone. Same with the usual open world Ubisoft trademarks such as outposts and viewpoints and such. Some may see that as a breath of fresh air, but for me I always was fond of those gameplay mechanics. Another issue is there's no progression tracker that's in every other open world Ubisoft game so you don't know how close you are to the end, how many side missions there are, etc. It adds a bit of mystery I guess but I would've rathered the usual mechanics. The hacking puzzles are much more in depth and involved than the first game which is much more enjoyable and requires more thinking through them, though they are still just maze puzzles. There's a lot more funny things you can do through hacking around the world as well. The world itself is much bigger than Chicago and way more colorful and alive than the first game, which was very grey and too serious. The online is also much more improved the first game as well and co-op partners can appear throughout the world at any time doing whatever they're doing in their own games. This can lead to fun and funny♥♥♥♥♥♥going on around the city. However even with these changes I still think this is a very good game, an 8 out of 10, better than the first game and personally more enjoyable than GTA V. If you think 60 is too much, I think that is fair, however I think 40 is more than fair for this game.
